newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, April still in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up, April still in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Thursday in a moderate session, but prices remained in recent ranges, with little reason to break far in either direction, sources said.
April climbed 10.4 cents to close at $1.839 per million British thermal units. May settled 5.1 cents higher at $1.953. Other deferreds ended up by one to 4.5 cents.

"The charts are looking more constructive. There's been good buying in the $1.80 area (basis April), but there are not enough fundamentals to take us much higher," said one trader, adding prices were consolidating after a two-month downtrend.
While forecasts for colder northern tier weather next helped boost the complex today, few saw much upside, with storage still comfortable and milder spring temperatures just around the corner.

Technical traders said April was likely to drift between $1.80 and $2.00 until cooling loads kick in to pick up the slack. They said an April close below $1.80 could lead to a test of the $1.701 contract low. Resistance also was at $2.04.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped almost a dime Thursday to the low-$1.80s. Midcon pipes were off more than a nickel to the mid-$1.70s. New York city gate swing gas was steady to higher in the $2.20s.
The 12-month strip gained 3.5 cents to $2.066. NYMEX said an estimated 30,939 Hub contracts traded, down from Wednesday's revised tally of 44,128.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Thursday.
On the KCBT, April finished six cents higher at $1.65, while deferreds ended up by three to six cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.3 cents to 23.6 cents (NYMEX premium).
